reason: E3 shows that as-cast eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1 already forms a fine lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure with high strength and ductility, so the premise that directional solidification is needed to create this structure is unsupported and the claimed improvements over the as-cast state are not evidenced. E4 describes toughening mechanisms in a different alloy (CrMnFeCoNi) and does not provide specific evidence for the claimed modulus increase or fracture resistance in AlCoCrFeNi2.1. E5 addresses a different alloy system and does not support the specific claims.
premises: Directional solidification of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 can produce a fine, regular lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure with ~1 μm spacing
A fine lamellar dual-phase structure increases yield strength by ~20% and ductility by ~15% relative to coarse as-cast state
The lamellar architecture increases Young's modulus by ~10% via load partitioning
The dual-phase structure enhances fracture resistance through crack bridging and deflection
